Keeping peptides cool in Murrieta

No NOAA normals station sits inside Murrieta, and the two nearest bracket the city. Fallbrook 5 NE is about 9 miles south at 1,140 feet; Elsinore is about 12 miles northwest at 1,268 feet.7112 The ground at the city's Census center point sits at about 1,237 feet.122

The two stations differ sharply. Fallbrook averages about 60 days a year at 90 °F or more and about 9 at 100 °F or more, with an August normal high of 89.3 °F.87 Its temperature normals rest on only 12 to 13 years of data.78 Elsinore averages about 123 days at 90 °F or more and about 42 at 100 °F or more, with a June to August normal high of 94.8 °F.11 Plan for the hotter figure in summer.

Rain falls mostly in winter. Fallbrook averages 15.31 inches a year, with 3.17 inches in January and only 0.08 to 0.22 inches a month from June to September.78

Dry air outside does not keep a vial dry inside. Peptides tend to be hygroscopic, meaning they pull water out of the air.910 Bachem advises letting a cold container reach room temperature in a desiccator before opening it, because absorbed moisture lowers the peptide content of the powder and may lower its stability.910 GenScript adds that peptides containing Asp, Glu, Lys, Arg or His are especially prone to absorbing moisture and should be kept in a desiccator in a tightly capped vial.13 Both makers advise taking out only what is needed, quickly, and resealing the container tightly.913 The storage guide covers temperatures, and the reconstitution guide covers the lab steps after that.

About Murrieta

Murrieta had 114,124 residents on July 1, 2025, sixth among the county's 28 incorporated cities and just behind Temecula.1 It covers 35.398 square miles of land.2 When it incorporated on July 1, 1991, it already had more than 24,000 residents, up from an estimated 2,200 in 1980.45

The city's history page says Juan Murrieta brought a flock of some 100,000 sheep to the valley in 1873, and that the trains serving the valley stopped running in 1935.4 The valley's natural hot springs made the Murrieta Hot Springs Resort well known in the first half of the 1900s.4 A drive of about 4 miles southwest from the Clinton Keith Road exit off Interstate 15 leads to the Santa Rosa Plateau Ecological Reserve, about 7,500 acres of oak woodland, chaparral and native grassland.3

Health care leads the city's employers. Southwest Healthcare's Rancho Springs Medical Center was the largest in 2025, with 2,399 employees, and Loma Linda University Medical Center ranked third with 1,514.5 Among working residents, 26.1% are in educational services, health care and social assistance, against 21.2% countywide.1415 The city's financial report describes the Murrieta Innovation Center as a hub for biotechnology, medical technology and entrepreneurship, and an expansion backed by the U.S. Department of Commerce and Riverside County is adding a new wet lab.5

Nearby

Temecula is about 6 miles south-southeast and Menifee about 8 miles north. The county hub, Peptides in Riverside, is about 28 miles north-northwest.2 Lakeland Village, Hemet, Temescal Valley and Valle Vista also have pages. Wildomar, about 5 miles northwest, and Lake Elsinore, about 11 miles northwest, have no page of their own.2

Frequently asked questions

Is Murrieta part of Temecula?

No. The two are neighbors about 6 miles apart.2 Land sold in the 1960s to develop Rancho California, a master-planned area, is known today as the cities of Temecula and Murrieta.3 Murrieta became its own city on July 1, 1991, after voters approved cityhood in November 1990.45 For an order it makes no difference: each city has its own page, and an address in either ships from the USA and Canada the same way. The neighboring page is Peptides in Temecula.

Which ZIP codes cover Murrieta?

Mainly 92562, with about 62% of the city's land, and 92563, with about 37%. A sliver of 92591, which is mostly Temecula, also falls inside city limits.6 About 81% of the land in 92562 lies outside any city or census-designated place, so that ZIP Code reaches well beyond city limits.6 All of them are served the same way, from the USA and Canada; the shipping page explains how ship-from origins work.

Does Murrieta's dry summer keep peptide powder dry?

Only until a cold vial is opened. Summer rain is scarce: the Fallbrook 5 NE station averages just 0.08 to 0.22 inches a month from June to September.78 Peptides tend to absorb water from the air, though, so Bachem advises letting a cold container reach room temperature in a desiccator before opening it. Absorbed moisture lowers the peptide content of the powder and may lower its stability.910
